title: Ward 4
draft: Claude's draft 2026-10-17 from story_script_v1 §6 (3.2: immobile with a broken wrist; the nurse from the bus; a sealed section, 'do not enter'; Ravi in the next bed, concussed, talking), ADR-37 (the 'acute viral encephalitis' cover-up; monsoon drains spread it during Act 3, off-screen, on the ward TV), infected_behaviour_v1 (light hurts them; noise draws them — planted, never explained), 1.5 (the bus nurse, HEBBAL in red on her badge, nurse_heard), 2.5 (ravi_supported / ravi_left), 3.1 (AMR-07, night_ops, the held card). The user edits the words and the numbers; then P18 builds it.
time: 10:20 the morning after the crash (3.1's card lands here); one day, no sleep in this scene
player_goal: Wake up in a government ward with your wrist in a cast; find out where you are and who is in the next bed.
design_goal: Curiosity after the shock (Act 3's quiet middle): you cannot leave, you can barely carry anything, and the ward is full of small wrong things — a nurse you've met before, a glass door at the end with the lights off behind it, a TV that keeps saying 'viral'. Ravi, concussed, talks in loops, and the loop keeps coming back to one sentence: 'Appa called. I answered.' That sentence is the door into 3.3, the flashback.

cast.role: The nurse from the 335-E bus (1.5), on day shift. Her badge reads SISTER LALITHA · HEBBAL GENERAL. If you talked on the bus (nurse_heard): 'You. The Cubbon bus. You let me sleep.' Else: 'You've got a face I've seen.' Then: 'Stay this side of the red line. That door is isolation. Nobody goes in, nobody asks.' She is kind, quick, and does not answer questions about the ward at the end.

In the next bed, head bandaged, concussed. He doesn't remember the junction. He talks in loops — the stipend 'still processing', his sister's wedding, 'they'll dock me for the bike'. If ravi_supported: 'You came at 1 AM. Nobody comes at 1 AM.' If ravi_left: he doesn't mention that night at all. Every loop ends nearer one sentence: 'Appa called. That night. I answered. You're supposed to change gloves first.' Then he stops.

beats.what: 3.1's held card gets its landing: 'HEBBAL GENERAL · WARD 4 · 10:20' and the ward fades in, you on your bed. A toast: 'Left wrist: fractured. Cast, six weeks.' The phone has been buzzing all night: Amma ('Where are you? Call me.' — one bar, the call won't connect), Sameer ('my bike?? forget the bike. are YOU ok' / without his bike: 'heard about the scooter. coming tomorrow'), Divya ('HR says take the week. Don't worry about AMR-07. Really.').
The nurse at her station: the bus callback, the red line on the floor, 'that door is isolation'. A tray by your bed (idli, cold) refills food once.

The end of the ward: a glass door taped over with newspaper, DO NOT ENTER in marker. The ward is lit; behind the glass the lights are off. Stand there and something on the other side taps on the glass — slow, patient — and stops when you step back. (Optional) The ward TV on the wall: 'Acute viral encephalitis: BBMP to clear storm drains before the monsoon. Officials: no cause for alarm.'

Ravi in the next bed: three loops of the same conversation (the stipend, the bike, the wedding loan), each one ending closer to 'Appa called. That night. I answered.' On the third he says it, and stops. The ward stays playable; 3.3 'The Corridor' starts from this line when it is built.

exits.note: lockedText 'Not discharged.' — the ward door opens in 3.5 Discharge
